title: eval-harness: add prompt-set regression CI hooks and quality gating for canary + main
author: Ethan Park
description:
Motivation: Prevent prompt-set regressions from reaching production and make eval gating an enforceable CI check across canary and main branches. This PR introduces new CI hooks that run the eval-harness prompt regression suite (fast subset) as a required check on canary and a full quality gate on main.

What this changes: adds a lightweight eval job to the GitHub Actions workflow for PRs against canary, adds a separate longer-running "eval-quality-gate" job for merges into main, and wires the results into status checks used by branch protection rules. The implementation includes: (1) a shared test runner script that parallelizes prompt-set shards and uploads aggregated metrics to the eval dashboard, (2) a diff-aware selector that runs only affected prompt sets when possible, (3) a configurable threshold file for per-prompt tolerances, and (4) clear failure messaging with links to the failing prompt examples and metric deltas.

Backwards compatibility: default thresholds are conservative and stored in eval/thresholds/default.json; teams can opt into stricter checks by adding per-directory threshold overrides.

Testing: included unit tests for the diff selector and integration tests that mock model outputs to validate gating behavior. CI demonstrated an initial failing run due to a brittle prompt expectation which was corrected in a follow-up commit.

Related: ENG-9843 (evaluation infra), ENG-9901 (quality gating), SUP-1123 (customer issue requesting regression protection).
